mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'the difference between the number of X and Y' as the signed subtraction X − Y, preserving the order of the names, rather than as an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes 'the difference between the number of ... and ...' without specifying a magnitude.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'the difference between the number of apples and oranges' as |apples − oranges| instead of apples − oranges.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements like 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B − N), preserving the sign of N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement directly compares two persons with a numeric offset.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 5 fewer items than B' as A = B + 5 instead of A = B − 5.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement 'A has N items' appears, set A’s current count to N at that moment, overwriting any previous value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement provides an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Treating a later direct count as immutable and ignoring a subsequent transfer that changes the count.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the given order; apply each transfer immediately before evaluating any later relational statements, so later statements see the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer statement appears before other statements that involve the same persons.
mathgap.example: Delaying the effect of a transfer until after a relational statement that depends on the transferred amount, causing the equation to use outdated values.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, translate them into (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of Y that C and D have.'
mathgap.example: Converting 'A has more than B equals C minus D' into A = B + (C − D) instead of (A − B) = (C − D).

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person 'eats N' of an item, subtract N from their count; when it says they multiply or double their items, apply the appropriate arithmetic operation.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement involves a person consuming or scaling their quantity.
mathgap.example: Forgetting to subtract when a person 'eats 3' items, leaving the count unchanged.

mathgap.title: Temporal Snapshot for Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Treat each relational statement as a constraint on the counts at the moment it appears; later changes to counts do not retroactively affect that constraint.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a relational statement that references current counts.
mathgap.example: Assuming a relational equation holds for final counts after later transfers, rather than for the snapshot at its position.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer of All Items
mathgap.principle: If a transfer statement says a person gives all their items to another, set the giver’s count to zero after the transfer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer explicitly mentions giving all items.
mathgap.example: Leaving the giver’s count unchanged after a 'gives all' transfer.

mathgap.title: Complete Statement Extraction
mathgap.principle: Extract every statement about the target item (direct counts, differences, transfers, equality of differences) before solving, ensuring no relevant constraint is omitted.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, to collect all information.
mathgap.example: Skipping a statement about a person’s count, resulting in an underdetermined system.

mathgap.title: Transfer with Unconstrained Giver
mathgap.principle: When a transfer involves a giver whose count is not otherwise constrained by any other statements, you can treat the giver’s count as a free variable and focus on the receiver’s updated count; the giver’s exact value is irrelevant for solving the queried variable.
mathgap.when_to_apply: During processing of a transfer, if the giver never appears in any other direct count, difference, or equality that influences the queried person.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve for the giver’s exact count after a transfer, even though the giver is never referenced elsewhere, leading to unnecessary equations.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to the common interpretation of ‘difference’ as magnitude, ignoring the order of the two names.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two names and compute X − Y, not |X − Y|.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as a separate phase rather than as immediate updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer instantly when it appears, before processing any later statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts are immutable initial conditions.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Update the person’s count whenever a later transfer or modification occurs; direct counts set the current value at that moment.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model simplifies the equation incorrectly, dropping one side of the equality.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate equality of differences into (A − B) = (C − D) and keep both sides.

mathgap.description: Incomplete processing of problem statements: stopping after a subset of constraints or ignoring many statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may stop early due to time constraints or misreading the problem length.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Systematically extract and incorporate every statement before solving.
